Definition: properly, to breathe hard, i.e. (by implication) to sigh
BiblicalUsage: Yâphach means to breathe hard, to gasp or sigh in distress. Jeremiah hears the voice of the daughter of Zion bewailing herself, wearied because of murderers, her breath coming hard with grief.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God hears the gasp of the grieving, and a sigh in Zion is a prayer He understands.
